items.text: 18 May 1973 — Recalling inverse and direct image
\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*G,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,f_*F)\qquad f^*\dashv f_*
$f^*$: left adjoint, commutes with direct limits, and left exact: hence exact. $f_*$: left exact only, but commutes with all inverse limits.
(f_*F)(U)=F\bigl(f^{-1}U\bigr)\qquad f^*G=G\times_Y X\ \ (\text{étale spaces})
Two special cases
(a) $X=\{x\}$ a point, $i_y\colon\{y\}\to Y$ the inclusion.
i_y^{*}F=F_y\qquad\text{(fibre of the étale space over } y)
So $f^*$ is a stalk functor relative to a map: same exactness as stalks.
(b) $f\colon X\to Y$ étale: $X$ is an object of $\operatorname{Top}(Y)$.
Composite of étale maps is étale: étale spaces over $X$ = étale spaces over $Y$ with a map to $X$.
C/X:\ \text{objects } X'\to X;\quad \operatorname{Top}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Top}(Y)/X
f^*G=G\times_Y X=G\times X\quad\text{(product in } \operatorname{Top}(Y),\ Y\text{ final)}
For an arrow $g\colon X'\to X$ in $\operatorname{Top}(Y)$:
g^*\colon \operatorname{Top}(Y)/X\to\operatorname{Top}(Y)/X',\qquad F\mapsto F\times_X X'
Notation: write the object $X'$ and forget the structure arrow $g$ — what people do, though less rigorous.
Algebraic structures and $f_*$, $f^*$
$f_*$ commutes with inverse limits: sheaves of groups, rings, modules go to the same.
Torsors are not preserved by $f_*$ (direct limits involved).
$f^*$ commutes with direct limits and finite inverse limits: preserves all such structures.
$f^*$(torsor under $G$) = torsor under $f^*G$; $f^*$(comodules over $A$) = comodules over $f^*A$.
Fields and integral domains, completed
Last time stuck; now the construction.
$A$ a ring object in $C$ (finite inverse limits and some sums). First the units.
A^{*}(Z)=A(Z)^{\times}\subset A(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(Z,A)
Subfunctor, a group functor; representable if fibre products exist:
A^{*}=\{(x,y)\in A\times A:\ xy=1\},\qquad A^*\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{pr}_1\ }A
\begin{CD} A^{*} @>>> \{*\}\\ @VVV @VV{1}V\\ A\times A @>{m}>> A \end{CD}
A field object
In sets: every element is invertible or zero. With $e$ the final object:
e\sqcup A^{*}\ \xrightarrow{\ (0,\ \mathrm{incl})\ }\ A\qquad\text{is an isomorphism}
Definition of a field object: this arrow is an isomorphism (in sheaves it is already a monomorphism).
An integral domain object
Sets: $A\neq 0$ and $xy=0\Rightarrow x=0$ or $y=0$.
For a sheaf of rings: not « $x=0$ or $y=0$ », but locally one or the other, depending on the point.
C=\{(x,y)\in A\times A: xy=0\}\quad\text{(the two coordinate axes)}
A\xrightarrow{x\mapsto(x,0)}C,\qquad A\xrightarrow{x\mapsto(0,x)}C
A\sqcup A\longrightarrow C\quad\text{epimorphism}
Epi $\iff$ cocartesian $\iff$ another arrow is an isomorphism.
Second axiom, $0\neq 1$: take $e'$ the kernel of $0,1\colon e\rightrightarrows A$.
In sheaves: the largest open set where $A=0$, the complement of the support.
\varnothing\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }e'\qquad(\varnothing\ \text{initial object})
Axioms: arrows built from finite inverse limits and some direct limits are isomorphisms.
Universal rings, domains, fields live on a classifying topos.
Also expressible: normal ring (integrally closed), reduced, connected spectrum. Regular: not tried.
A sheaf of fields is never a presheaf of fields: $F(U\sqcup V)=F(U)\times F(V)$, and $F(\varnothing)=\{*\}$ is not a field.
Check diagrammatic axioms on stalks: a sheaf of rings is a sheaf of fields iff its stalks are fields.
Constant sheaves
$f\colon X\to\{*\}$; $f^*\colon\mathbf{Sets}\to\operatorname{Top}(X)$.
I_X=f^*I=I\times X=\coprod_{i\in I}X\quad\text{(étale space over } X)
If $I$ is a group, ring, field...: $I_X$ is a constant sheaf of groups, of rings, of fields.
Meromorphic functions
$X$ a reduced, locally irreducible complex analytic space; $\mathcal M_X(U)$ = meromorphic functions on $U$.
Locally a quotient of holomorphic functions, denominator not identically zero near any point.
\mathcal M_{X,x}=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_{X,x})\quad\text{a field}
So $\mathcal M_X$ is a sheaf of fields, not constant (stalks vary, not canonically isomorphic).
Algebraic geometry: rational functions on an integral scheme — a constant sheaf of fields.
Internal Hom
So far: limit constructions. Now a new construction. $F$, $G$ sheaves on $X$.
$\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)$ = the set of morphisms; underlined = a sheaf:
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F,G)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}(F|_U,\,G|_U)
Restriction to $V\subset U$ is clear: a presheaf; and it is a sheaf (to be seen).
